meta_title: CacheTrace · Cache memory simulator, calculator and practice exams
meta_desc: Simulate cache memory instruction by instruction, work out block, line, set and tag tables, and practice with exams graded instantly. Direct-mapped, 2-way and 4-way set-associative, and fully associative. Free and open source.
lead: Simulate execution instruction by instruction, work out the tables of your exercises, and practice with exams that grade themselves. Direct-mapped, 2-way and 4-way set-associative, and fully associative.
hero_meta: Browser · No installation · No servers · MIT license
stat1: cache organizations for the same program
stat3: practice activities with hints, grading and a PDF solution
t_title: Three ways to understand the cache.
t_sub: From a whole program to an exam exercise: pick the one you need.
tc1_p: Run a program with loops, lw, sw, lb, sb… and replay every Fetch and Execute on the four caches.
tc1_a: Cache and register state step by step
tc2_p: Enter the data of an exercise (addresses, accesses, initial state) and get the solved tables.
tc2_a: Block, offset, range, line or set, and tag
tc2_b: LW and SW access traces on the four variants
tc2_c: A set with write-back and the range written
tc3_p: Three exams per difficulty with the usual cache exercise types, graded instantly.
tc3_a: A lightbulb hint in every activity
tc3_c: Download the solution as a PDF
f_title: Everything about cache, in one place.
f_sub: Simulate, calculate and practice with the same rules, checked by tests.
c1_p: The same program is replayed on direct-mapped, 2-way, 4-way and fully associative caches, with a comparison of hits and evictions.
c2_p: Every address is split into tag, index and offset with fixed colours, derived from the address bus, the cache size and the block size.
c3_p: Every instruction produces a Fetch; memory instructions add their data access. Step through the program and inspect the cache and registers.
c4_p: Addresses, blocks, LW and SW traces, and a set resolved with write-back, with tables ready to compare against your own solution.
c5_p: Every activity has a hint with the method and the formulas. Grading accepts 0x204, 0X204 or 204 as the same answer.
c6_p: The simulator exports an Excel workbook with formulas; every practice exam has its solution as a PDF.
p1: Each exam has ten activity types: diagnostics, placement, the four variants, comparison, errors, write-back and a final test
p2: Three levels: the easy one gives many cells; the hard one changes the parameters and gives almost nothing
p3: A lightbulb button in every activity explains the method and the formulas without giving the answer
p4: Tolerant grading for upper case, prefixes and formats; cells turn green or red
p5: At the end, download the PDF solution with the solved tables and how each result is obtained
p_note: The exercises are original and their solutions are computed with the same verified engine as the calculator.
pm_hint: Write the block in binary in groups of 4 digits. In direct mapping, the line is the last bits of the block and the tag is the rest.
x_title: An Excel with formulas, not screenshots.
x1: One sheet per organization: DM, SA2W, SA4W and FA, whichever you choose
x2: Tag, index and offset bits computed with formulas from the address
x3: Final cache state with bytes D0–D7 and instructions shown as I_n
x4: Evolution sheets for the cache and the registers after every instruction
x5: A Statement sheet with the parameters, the program and the dump
x_note: The .xlsx workbooks open in Excel and LibreOffice. Evolution sheets are optional.
w_title: From the idea to the table in three steps.
s1_p: The simulator for whole programs, the calculator for single exercises and the practice exams to train.
s2_p: Memory, cache and block with their unit; then the program and the dump, or the accesses of the exercise.
s3_p: Step through the result, compare it with your solution, export to Excel or grade your practice exam.
m_sub: CacheTrace always applies the same rules and documents them, so you can check the result against your own problem statement.
m2: invalid lines are filled in order
p1_c: The tools' interface is currently in Spanish
p1_d: .xlsx workbooks open in Excel and LibreOffice
p2_p: CacheTrace is a study tool. It models a unified cache with a fixed write policy; it does not replace a hardware simulator or the official solution to your course. Always check the results against your own problem statement.
fin_sub: No sign-up, MIT license. Try the simulator or start a practice exam.
foot_desc: Cache memory simulator, calculator and practice exams for computer architecture.
foot_made: What you enter is processed in your browser
